item.title: 2027: INEC seeks inclusive polls, sensitises PWDs, Electoral Officers in Benue
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Benue State has held a sensitisation workshop for Persons With Disabilities (PWDs), Electoral Officers (EOs) and Disability Desk Officers, targeting improved accessibility, effective deployment of assistive devices and inclusive participation in the 2027 general elections. The workshop, organised by the commission ahead of the elections, was designed to strengthen stakeholders’ understanding of disability inclusion, electoral rights and interventions aimed at ensuring that eligible voters with disabilities can participate fully in the electoral process. Speaking at the event, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Benue State, Mallam Aminu Idris, said INEC was committed to engaging stakeholders to ensure the conduct of free, fair and credible elections, stressing that inclusivity was equally essential to achieving that objective. The REC said, “it is not just to have free, fair and credible elections. It is to have inclusive elections. If you leave a chunk of your population out, you cannot be talking about free, fair and credible elections.” He added that INEC had a dedicated department responsible for inclusivity and addressing the concerns of disadvantaged groups to ensure everyone had the opportunity to participate in the electoral process. He explained that the commission identifies voters with disabilities during registration to enable it determine the needs of different polling units and deploy appropriate materials and assistance noting that “the objective is to ensure that eligible voters who have registered and obtained their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) did not encounter unnecessary difficulties while voting.” On the participation of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), the REC disclosed that INEC had conducted registration exercises at IDP locations in collaboration with non-governmental organisations interested in encouraging voter registration. He said “our officials visited the locations on two consecutive days to register eligible voters to ensure that they exercise their franchise during the election.” Addressing concerns over the collection of PVCs, Idris said “cards belonging to those who registered during the first phase of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise, conducted between August and December 2025, are available for collection at the local government level.” He added that cards for those who registered in 2026 would be ready subsequently before the elections. In his goodwill message, the Benue State Director of the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Comrade Mark Dewua, commended INEC for the initiative, saying “inclusive electoral participation is essential to strengthening democracy.” He urged for “accessible polling units, effective communication of electoral information, appropriate deployment of assistive devices and respectful treatment of voters with disabilities.” Dewua, who reaffirmed NOA’s commitment to collaborating with

item.title: 2027: INEC puts preliminary voters’ register online, publishes final document Dec. 15
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has made the Preliminary Register of Voters for the 2027 General Election available on its online platform, following concerns raised by some stakeholders and in preparation for the certification and publication of the Final Register of Voters on December 15. The register can now be accessed at https://display.inecnigeria.org. It is the same list that was earlier displayed at Registration Areas nationwide. National Commissioner and Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee at INEC, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, said in a statement on Monday that the Commission “has taken note of the concerns expressed by Nigerians and other stakeholders regarding the desirability of making the Register accessible through its online platform in addition to the physical display already conducted.” “Accordingly, and in furtherance of its commitment to transparency, accessibility and public confidence in the electoral process, the Commission has decided to make available on its online platform https://display.inecnigeria.org the same Preliminary Register of Voters earlier displayed at the Registration Areas,” he said. Haruna recalled that the physical display was held in accordance with Section 19 of the Electoral Act, 2026, from 9th to 15th October, 2026. According to him, the exercise provided “registered voters the opportunity to inspect their particulars and submit claims and objections as prescribed by law.” He said the online publication does not replace the exercise already carried out. “This additional measure complements the physical display already undertaken and is intended to facilitate wider public access to the Register,” he said. The Commission said it is still processing the claims and objections that arose from the display. “Meanwhile, the Commission continues to process claims and objections arising from the exercise in accordance with the Electoral Act, 2026, preparatory to the certification and publication of the Final Register of Voters on 15th December 2026. “The Commission appreciates the continued interest and constructive engagement of Nigerians and stakeholders and reiterates its commitment to transparency, accountability and the faithful implementation of the Electoral Act, 2026 in delivering credible elections,” he said. item.title: Prof. Ochefu rejects appointment to NDC National Campaign Council
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi Professor of Economic History and Strategic Studies at Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi, Prof. Yakubu Ochefu, has rejected his purported appointment to the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) National Campaign Council, insisting that he is not a member of the party. Ochefu said he was neither consulted before his name was included in the list of members of the campaign council circulating on social media nor did he give his consent to the appointment. The university don, who is also the National Chairman of the Association of Nigerian Universities Alumni (ANUA) and President-General of Ochetoha K’Idoma, said his leadership positions required him to remain non-partisan, as the memberships of both organisations cut across political parties. In a statement he personally signed, Prof. Ochefu said, “My attention has been drawn to a list circulating on social media, titled ‘Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) National Campaign Council’, which names me as a member of its National Campaign Caucus. “I wish to inform the public that I am not a member of the NDC and have never been. “I was not consulted before my name was included, nor did I give consent. “I have written to the Chairman of the Council to decline the appointment and to request that my name be withdrawn and a revised list published. “As National Chairman of the Association of Nigerian Universities Alumni, ANUA, and President-General of Ochetoha K’Idoma, I lead organisations whose members cut across all political parties. These offices require me to remain non-partisan, and I intend to honour that obligation. “I thank all who reached out for clarification, and ask that you disregard the list insofar as it concerns me.” The post Prof. Ochefu rejects appointment to NDC National Campaign Council appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ADC to APC: Nigerians suffer, your youth leaders ride N1bn SUVs
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has slammed the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, over the reported distribution of seven luxury sports utility vehicles (SUVs) worth about N1 billion to its youth leaders, accusing the ruling party of prioritising political mobilisation over the hardship facing Nigerians. The opposition party said the reported distribution exposed the contradiction between the economic sacrifices Nigerians are being asked to make and the privileges enjoyed by the ruling party’s political operatives, with millions struggling to afford food, transportation and other necessities. In a statement on Monday, ADC National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, said the development raised questions about the APC’s priorities as it prepares for the 2027 general elections. “President Tinubu asks Nigerians to endure hardship while his party distributes luxury vehicles to its political operatives. Apparently, sacrifice is for ordinary Nigerians, while luxury is reserved for those working to keep the APC in power,” he said. Abdullahi said the ruling party had mobilised resources for its political machinery without offering a convincing answer to the rising cost of living. “The APC has found the resources to move its campaign officials around Nigeria. What it has failed to find is a convincing way to make life affordable for the Nigerians whose votes it now seeks,” he said. The ADC also questioned the rationale for providing the vehicles for grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections when youth unemployment and economic hardship remain major concerns. “Seven APC youth leaders can receive luxury vehicles, but millions of young Nigerians are still waiting for the jobs, opportunities and economic relief they were promised. Is this the APC’s idea of youth empowerment?” Abdullahi asked. The party demanded disclosure of the source of funding for the vehicles, including whether public resources were involved. “Nigerians deserve to know who paid for these vehicles. Until that question is answered, the ruling party cannot dismiss legitimate concerns about its priorities,” Abdullahi said. item.title: ADC fires back at APC over unpaid salary claims
item.description: dares ruling party to defend record By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has challenged the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to defend its record in government rather than make allegations against opposition parties, dismissing claims of unpaid salaries within the ADC as false and politically motivated. The party said the allegation was an attempt to divert attention from the economic hardship, rising cost of living, unemployment and insecurity confronting Nigerians, warning that the 2027 election debate should centre on the Tinubu administration’s performance. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC challenged the APC Presidential Campaign Council to produce evidence to substantiate its allegation, describing the claim as an attempt to distract Nigerians from the government’s record. “If the APC has any credible evidence to support its claims, it should produce it rather than continue to insult Nigerians with fabricated stories masquerading as press statements,” Abdullahi said. On the issues it believes should dominate public debate, the ADC said: “The real issue is the cost of living. The real issue is the absence of jobs and opportunities for our young people. The real issue is the insecurity that continues to threaten lives, livelihoods, and communities across the country.” The party also accused the APC of preparing for the 2027 elections by attacking opposition parties rather than presenting its achievements. “It is becoming increasingly clear that the APC has decided to run its 2027 campaign on allegations against the opposition rather than achievements of its own. That is what happens when a government has spent years making promises it cannot keep and excuses it cannot defend,” Abdullahi said. The ADC spokesman urged Minister of Information, Alake, and other APC officials to explain why Nigerians should support another term for the ruling party after three years of economic hardship and insecurity. “The APC may control the machinery of government, but it cannot control the lived experiences of Nigerians,” he said. Abdullahi said the ADC would remain focused on holding the Tinubu administration accountable, insisting that allegations against the opposition would not displace the economic concerns shaping public debate. “If the APC has a record to defend, let it defend it. If it has solutions, let it present them. But it should stop insulting the intelligence of Nigerians with these increasingly desperate distractions,” he added. The party maintained that the cost of living would remain central to its campaign, positioning the economic consequences of the Tinubu administration’s policies as a defining issue in the 2027 election. item.title: Mass killing threat: Enugu ex-lawmakers place N5m bounty on terrorist ringleaders
item.description: By Precious Enaike The Chairman of the forum of former members of Enugu State House of Assembly, Dr. Josef Onoh, announced Monday that they have placed a bounty of N5m on terrorists threatening mass killings in Enugu State after watching a viral video containing treasonable, cowardly and bloodthirsty threats of invasion against the peaceful domain of the state. These threats, Onoh said, issued by terrorists masquerading under whatever deceitful umbrella or criminal guise they claim, represent an intolerable assault on the collective security, sovereignty, and peace. Speaking on behalf of the Forum, in Abuja, Onoh categorically condemned the provocative rhetoric in the strongest possible terms and made it known clearly and unequivocally to the miscreants that Enugu State is not, and will never become, a playground for terrorists, bandits, or extremist agitators. According to him, stakeholders have built a heritage of peace, and no masked cowards chanting death threats will be allowed to disrupt the lives of the people. Onoh said the security of Enugu State remains paramount, and the forum will not fold its arms while fringe criminals attempt to intimidate our citizens or destabilize our homeland. “The forum stands resolutely behind the Enugu State Government and security agencies to crush any attempt at violating the peace of the state. To accelerate the wheels of justice and unmask every single criminal hiding under these guises, I have, on behalf of the forum of former members of Enugu State House of Assembly announced the strategic rewards of N5,000,000 (Five Million Naira) bounty for anyone who provides credible, actionable information to the Department of State Services (DSS), the Nigeria Police Force, or any other security agencies that leads directly to the arrest and prosecution of the main character chanting the death threats in the video, as well as any of his co-conspirators. “Furthermore, I would place a N50,000 (Fifty Thousand Naira) reward per name to any patriotic citizen who provides the full names and verified identities of each individual appearing in the video, along with details of their relatives, to the security agencies. I urge the DSS and all sister security apparatuses to launch an immediate, aggressive manhunt for the criminals. “To the good people of Enugu State, I urge them to remain calm, vigilant, and resilient and not be intimidated by the desperate rants of cowards while also reporting any suspicious movements or individuals to the nearest security agency immediately. Let me make it clear that Enugu State belongs to the peaceful and law-abiding individuals and forces of terror will always be defeated,” Onoh said. item.title: 5 prominent Obidient members missing from NDC presidential campaign council
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has unveiled its 2027 presidential campaign council, naming flagbearer, Peter Obi and National Leader Seriake Dickson among its leaders. However, several prominent members of the Obidient movement who have actively and publicly supported Obi in the past are absent from the published list. The absence of such individuals is notable because they have either supported the NDC presidential candidate or taken part in the political movement in different ways, with their public profiles ranging from campaign activism and digital mobilisation to formal movement leadership. The list the party published on Sunday names the campaign caucus, advisory council, directorates and state coordinators. It also includes Obi and other senior party figures, but omits a few influential figures who have actively backed the Obidient movement in recent years. Here are five prominent Obidient movement members omitted from the NDC 2027 presidential campaign council. 1 . Moses Paul (Dr. Mo) Moses Paul, popularly known as Dr. Mo, has held formal leadership roles in the Obidient movement. He was identified as its Secretary General in 2025 and appointed National Coordinator in October 2026, while his predecessor, Yunusa Tanko, took on a role as an adviser to Obi. Dr. Mo rose to national prominence as the convener of the Free Nigeria Movement and a key organizer of youth-led mobilization and rallies supporting Peter Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign under the Labour Party. Obi also publicly backed Paul’s bid for chairman of the Abuja Municipal Area Council, saying he would campaign for him. Paul’s omission from the released council list stands out given his current leadership role in the movement and his previous candidacy with Obi’s support. 2. Aisha Yesufu Campaign activist and NDC member Aisha Yesufu served on Obi’s 2023 Labor Party presidential campaign team and was one of the prominent public voices backing his candidacy. She has also described the Obidient movement as part of a broader wave of political engagement after the #EndSARS protests, rather than a movement created by Obi. In May 2026, Yesufu joined the NDC, saying her political choices had been guided by her support for Obi. She declared for the FCT Senate seat but later withdrew from the race after internal party decisions on primaries. Her absence from the campaign council is notable given her past campaign role, movement profile and NDC membership. 3. Precious Oruche (Mama Pee) Precious Oruche, popularly known as Mama Pee, is regularly identified in news reports as an Obidient activist, grassroots organizer, social influencer, and an outspoken supporter of Obi. In 2025, the movement publicly supported her after a reported incident involving factional Labour Party chairman Julius Abure. item.description: The rankings for the 2026 Ballon d’Or are being unveiled live on Monday, October 26, with several prominent footballers named among the players ranked 25th to 29th in the men’s category. Paris Saint-Germain captain Marquinhos, Bayern Munich defender Dayot Upamecano, Manchester United midfielder Bruno Fernandes, Al-Qadsiah forward Julian Quiñones and Arsenal defender William Saliba are among the players whose positions have been announced so far. According to updates from the official Ballon d’Or account, Marquinhos occupies 25th place, while Upamecano is ranked 26th and Fernandes takes 27th position. Quiñones is ranked 28th, with Saliba sharing 29th place in the standings. The rankings are being released as the ceremony unfolds, with football fans awaiting the announcement of the players who have made the top positions and the eventual winner of the prestigious individual award. The Ballon d’Or recognises the outstanding individual performances of footballers over the relevant assessment period, with players judged on their performances, achievements and overall contribution to the game. The ceremony is taking place in London, with England captain and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane among the leading contenders for the men’s award, alongside Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal and other leading stars. This report will be updated as more rankings and winners are announced. item.title: From Nigeria to Multiple Markets Across Borders: How SharpPunter Is Changing the Way Punters Analyse Sports
item.description: A typical Saturday slip in Nigeria is put together from several places at once: a booking code a tipster posted in a WhatsApp group with no explanation behind it, a few games a friend swore were safe, and, for many fans, their own club, added out of loyalty before anyone has checked its form. If the code was shared from a bookmaker the punter does not use, he first has to rebuild it on his own bookmaker by hand, one match at a time, and once it is placed, a single one of its twelve games going the wrong way is enough to take down the slip and every version of it shared around the group, a pattern that repeats with codes passed around in Accra, Nairobi and Douala. SharpPunter, a sports analysis platform built in Nigeria, was set up to give those punters a clearer look at what they are betting on before they place the slip. Six months after its launch in April 2026, it has users across West, East and Southern Africa, works with booking codes from 37 bookmakers and has just released V2, a rebuilt version of its app. Built in Nigeria, for the way Nigerians bet “I built SharpPunter because I was tired of seeing people stake their money on tips they had not checked by themselves, and I wanted something that would help punters truly understand which games were worth backing,” said Oluwatobi Abobade, who founded SharpPunter. “Over time, the way people use the product has shaped how we built V2. Users kept tagging our X bot with codes from friends, so checking a code is now one of the two things you see when you open the app. We also saw how closely people follow their own clubs and how often that turns their picks into emotional ones, so V2 lets you follow your club, get updates on its live matches and see the stats, alongside unbiased picks you can use.” Where slips go wrong, and what SharpPunter does about it The first problem is the tip itself, since most codes that circulate in group chats arrive with no rationale, and give punters no way to judge whether the picks are valid. Every SharpPunter pick shows the reasoning behind it, such as a team’s recent form or its record against that opponent, and carries a rating of Strong, Fair or Slim, and the Optimizer reads any code a user pastes in and rates each match SharpPunter covers. The second is the single weak game that usually sinks a whole accumulator, often across every variation of the slip a punter has placed. In V2, the Optimizer flags the weakest selections on a code and suggests swaps before the bet goes in, while the Shuffle tool deals the matches from several codes into balanced slips so that one bad pick cannot take all of them down. The third is the code that only works on one bookmaker, which leaves punters rebuilding a friend’s slip by hand, one match at a time. SharpPunter’s converter rebuilds the same matches on the punter’s own bookmaker, and it now supports conversions across 37 bookmakers. item.title: Why Africa Cannot abandon Cuba
item.description: BY FEMI FALANA SAN (Speech delivered at the Rally held by the Nigeria Solidarity Movement with Cuba in Lagos on October 24, 2026) INTRODUCTION Following the 1959 Cuban Revolution, Fidel Castro made solidarity with Africa a corner stone of the foreign policy of Cuba. Hence, the government developed interest in the anticolonial movements and socialist governments in Africa. In 1961, Cuba sent a military mission to the Kwame Nkrumah government in Ghana. And following the independence of Algeria in 1962, Cuba sent military assistance and medical supplies to the Algerian National Liberation Front. The visit of Ernesto Che Guevara to the progressive movements in the Portuguese colonies in 1964 consolidated the involvement of Cuba in African affairs. A year later, Che Guevara was in the Democratic Republic of the Congo to offer his knowledge and experience as a guerrilla fighter. CUBA’S SUPPORT FOR LIBERATION STRUGGLE IN AFRICA Cuba became a strong ally of the defunct Organization for African Unity and the African Union in the struggle against colonialism and apartheid. In justifying Cuba’s internationalist foreign policy and deployment of troops to support anti-colonial and anti-apartheid movements across Africa, Fidel Castro famously stated, “African blood flows freely through our veins. Many of our ancestors came as slaves from Africa to this land. As slaves they struggled a great deal. They fought as members of the Liberating Army of Cuba. We’re brothers and sisters of the people of Africa and we’re ready to fight on their behalf.” On another occasion, the Cuban leader said, “We are a Latin-American nation and a Latin-African nation as well.” In support of the independence movements that engaged in armed struggle against European colonial powers in Guinea-Bissau, Mozambique, and Angola, Cuba sent military advisers, fighters and equipment. Thousands of Cuban troops were deployed to support the People’s Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA) against the invading South African apartheid forces and rival local armed groups sided by the United States and other western governments. Not less than 55,000 Cuban troops took part in the historic battle of Cuito Cuanavale in Angola from 1987–1988. Indeed, it was the military setbacks suffered in the battle field by South Africa that compelled the apartheid regime to enter into the political negotiations that culminated in the independence of Namibia in 1990, and South Africa in 1994. CUBA’S MEDICAL INTERVENTIONS IN AFRICA Based on its long-standing history of medical internationalism in Africa, Cuba has sent thousands of medical personnel including doctors and nurses to confront dangerous diseases in many African countries. item.title: Atiku’s ADC owing salaries for over 12 months, APC PCC alleges
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has alleged that the African Democratic Congress ADC has not paid its staff salaries for more than 12 months, and urged Nigerians to reject the party and its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, in the next general elections. In a statement on Monday in Abuja by its Spokesperson, Dele Alake, the council said it had come to its attention that the ADC National Working Committee NWC, “led by Senator David Mark as Chairman and Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola as Secretary, has refused and neglected to pay party staff for over a year.” “We find it unconscionable that a political party that has made many grandiose promises to hoodwink Nigerians owes its workers for more than 12 months. Owing staff who come to work every day and who rely on the salaries for their daily sustenance is wicked and reprehensible”, APC added. The council said the development had exposed “the emptiness and insincerity of those parading themselves as ‘new saviours’.” It maintained that ADC leaders and their presidential candidate, Atiku, “do not mean well and can do nothing for our country.” According to the APC PCC, “Their desperation for power is driven by personal aggrandisement and venomous ill will against President Bola Tinubu. A party that cannot pay its cleaners and workforce cannot be entrusted with our country’s affairs.” The council also turned to Atiku’s record as an employer, saying he “has a reputation for owing his employees.” “While he regularly junkets to the UAE, staff at his Gotel Communication and other businesses also went months without pay and staged protests over unpaid salaries and other benefits,” the statement said. On Aregbesola, the council said his record “on paying workers’ salaries and pensioners in Osun State, where he was a governor for 8 years, was abysmal.” “As governor, he mismanaged the state’s finances to the point that he could not pay workers. His government thus introduced quarter-salary and, at times, half-salary payments. As for pensioners, he abandoned them for more than four years. Many died because they could not afford the basics of life”, the APC campaign added. The APC-PCC said it is therefore not surprised that ADC, harbouring birds of the same feather, cannot pay its workers’ salaries. The council then issued what it called a warning to Nigerians and working people: “reject ADC. Reject Atiku Abubakar and reject all ADC candidates in the next general elections. They do not have the interest of our country and our people at heart. “A party that aspires to govern Nigeria and which cannot be trusted with something as basic as the management of its own affairs and the welfare of its workforce should be rejected by Nigerians.” The post Atiku’s ADC owing salaries for over 12 months, APC PCC alleges appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Drop your ambition, back Tinubu, RMRDC boss tells Obi
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Director General and Chief Executive Officer of the Raw Materials Research and Development Council RMRDC, Prof. Nnanyelugo Ike-Muonso, has urged the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC, Mr Peter Obi, to shelve his ambition for the 2027 election and support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. Ike-Muonso, who spoke during an interactive session with reporters in Abuja, argued that the South should be allowed to complete its eight-year tenure before power returns to the North. He said the principle of power rotation between the North and South, which has shaped Nigeria’s political calculations since the return to democracy in 1999, should guide political actors as they prepare for the 2027 general elections. “Presidential ambition must be balanced with the larger interests of national unity, political stability and the need to sustain policies that can transform the economy. Nigeria has developed a political tradition of power rotation between the North and South, and respecting that understanding can help strengthen confidence among the country’s diverse political constituencies”, he said. While he conceded that the Constitution does not prescribe a North-South rotation of the presidency, he said the arrangement has, however, remained an important consideration among major parties and stakeholders seeking to manage regional interests and maintain national balance. Ike-Muonso said Obi should consider postponing his aspiration until after Tinubu’s second term, and after the North would have the opportunity to produce a President. He said this would serve political stability, national cohesion and continuity in governance. He also urged Obi to consider joining the All Progressives Congress APC. According to him, engagement within the ruling party would let the former Anambra State governor contribute to policy debates, understand its governance structures and take part in development programmes being implemented by APC-controlled states. Ike-Muonso said membership would also give Obi a chance to observe how the party’s state governments approach infrastructure, education, healthcare, investment and economic development. He acknowledged Obi’s following, saying: “Peter Obi has built a political following and brought issues of public expenditure, accountability and economic management into the national conversation. Those issues deserve sustained engagement. But political leadership also requires strategic decisions about when to contest, when to collaborate and how best to contribute to national development.” The RMRDC chief said Obi’s influence and support base could be deployed to promote constructive engagement on governance, economic development and institutional reforms, rather than concentrating exclusively on the immediate contest for the presidency. item.title: Nigeria could declare Ebola outbreak over by Dec 7 – Pate
item.description: By Sola Ogundipe Nigeria could declare the Ebola outbreak over as early as December 7, 2026, if no further confirmed or probable cases are detected following the medical evacuation of the country’s imported index patient. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Mohammed Ali Pate, disclosed the provisional date on Monday as health authorities intensified contact tracing, investigated suspected cases and strengthened preparedness across health facilities to prevent further spread of the Bundibugyo virus disease. Writing on his X handle, Pate said the 42-day countdown towards declaring the outbreak over would be subject to validation by the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) and the World Health Organisation (WHO), in line with established outbreak management criteria. The development follows the evacuation of Nigeria’s index patient to Switzerland for further medical care, a move that has heightened attention on the country’s capacity to sustain containment measures and prevent community transmission. According to Pate, “Following the imported Ebola index patient’s medical evacuation from Nigeria today, 26 October, our immediate priorities remain active monitoring of all identified contacts, prompt investigation of alerts and strengthened readiness across our health facilities. “If no further confirmed or probable cases are detected, Nigeria could progress towards declaring this outbreak over under @WHO criteria, potentially as early as 7 December 2026. This date remains provisional, subject to @NCDCgov and WHO validating the 42-day countdown. Any further case would require a fresh countdown in accordance with those criteria,” Pate noted. He said the proposed December 7 date is therefore not a final declaration that Nigeria is Ebola-free, but a conditional target that depends on the absence of further cases and the completion of the required surveillance period. Further, he said, “Our teams, working with FCTA and state health authorities and our partners, remain focused on containment and preventing community transmission. “I ask Nigerians to remain calm, cooperate with contact-tracing teams and follow regular updates from @NCDCgov and @Fmohnigeria.” The post Nigeria could declare Ebola outbreak over by Dec 7 – Pate appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Alleged N582m fraud: Court fixes Nov 23 for trial of ex-NNPCL boss
item.description: threatens to issue bench warrant By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Monday fixed November 23 for the arraignment of a former President of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) Staff Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society, Abuja, Mr. Olalekan Ogunbayo, over his alleged complicity in a ₦582 million fraud. The court, presided over by Justice Lesley Wike, further threatened to issue a bench warrant against the defendant should he fail to appear before it to enter his plea to an eight-count charge preferred against him by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). After the case was called, the anti-graft agency drew the court’s attention to the absence of the defendant, who was billed for arraignment. According to the prosecution, the development marked the third time the defendant had stayed away from court despite being aware of the case. EFCC’s lawyer, R. U. Adagba, who informed the court that only the 2nd defendant in the matter, Abolade Nurudeen, was available for the proceedings, alleged that Ogunbayo had jumped the administrative bail granted him by the Commission. He told the court that all efforts to locate the 1st defendant for service of the charge on him had been unsuccessful. Consequently, he applied for a bench warrant to be issued to enable security agencies to arrest and produce the defendant in court for trial. The prosecution counsel premised his application for the bench warrant on the provisions of Sections 35, 113 and 114 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) 2015. However, Mr. Innocent Adoo, who announced his appearance for the defendants, opposed the application. He accused the EFCC of failing to properly serve a copy of the charge on the defendant. The defence counsel argued that arraignment in a criminal trial cannot proceed without proper service of the charge on the defendant. He submitted that a defendant must be informed of the allegations against him and given adequate opportunity to prepare his defence, adding that service could not be waived by any party. Adoo told the court that Ogunbayo was still on administrative bail and was unaware of the scheduled arraignment. He explained that the defence had used the information available to it to communicate with Ogunbayo, who was said to be in Warri, Delta State, and unable to secure a flight to Abuja for the sitting. He therefore prayed the court for an adjournment to enable both defendants to appear and take their pleas in the interest of justice. In his ruling, Justice Wike held that, in the interest of justice, the matter should be adjourned to enable the first defendant to appear for arraignment. The judge, however, warned that the court would take the necessary steps if Ogunbayo failed to appear on the next adjourned date. item.title: Man swept away by flood while trying to rescue drowning teenager in Abia
item.description: . Rescue team in desperate search for duo By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — In a heartbreaking twist of fate, a good Samaritan who risked his life to save a teenage girl from a flooded gutter in Aba, Abia State, was swept away by the same rushing water alongside the girl he tried to rescue. The tragedy occurred on Sunday evening at Ukwu Mango, Faulks Road, during a downpour, leaving residents and sympathisers scrambling desperately to find the two missing persons. The Samaritan reportedly slipped into the gutter while attempting to rescue the girl, only for the surging floodwater to sweep both of them away. Residents immediately launched a frantic search, hoping to find the pair alive, but their efforts yielded no result, fuelling fears that the victims might have been carried into the Aba River. The desperate search entered a new phase on Monday as the Abia State Fire Service and other government officials joined residents in combing the drainage channels for the missing duo. Police personnel also arrived at the scene to control the crowd and maintain order as the rescue operation continued. However, as of the time of filing this report, the victims remained missing, leaving their families and the community in agonising uncertainty over their fate. When Vanguard contacted the Police Public Relations Officer, PPRO Maureen Chinaka, she promised to revert but had yet to do so at the time of filing this report. Aba’s flat terrain makes the commercial city prone to flooding, particularly during heavy rainfall. item.title: APC accuses ADC of owing staff salaries, urges Nigerians to reject Atiku
item.description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused the African Democratic Congress (ADC) of owing its workers more than 12 months’ salaries, urging Nigerians to reject the party, its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, and its candidates in the next general elections. The council’s spokesperson, Dele Alake, made the call in a statement, accusing the ADC National Working Committee, led by Senator David Mark as chairman and Rauf Aregbesola as secretary, of neglecting party workers despite their reliance on salaries for their daily needs. Alake described the alleged failure to pay the workers as “wicked and reprehensible”, questioning the party’s capacity to manage the country’s affairs if it could not meet its obligations to its own employees. “We find it unconscionable that a political party that has made many grandiose promises to hoodwink Nigerians owes its workers for more than 12 months,” he said. “Owing staff who come to work every day and who rely on the salaries for their daily sustenance is wicked and reprehensible.” The APC PCC spokesperson said the allegation exposed what he described as the insincerity of the ADC leadership, adding that Nigerians should reject the party at the polls. “We have clearly stated that ADC leaders and their presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, do not mean well and can do nothing for our country,” Alake said. He further alleged that Atiku had a history of failing to pay workers, claiming that employees of Gotel Communication and other businesses linked to the former vice-president had previously gone months without salaries and staged protests over unpaid wages and other benefits. Alake also criticised Aregbesola’s record as governor of Osun State, alleging that his administration struggled to pay workers and pensioners during his eight-year tenure. He said the state government had introduced quarter-salary and, at times, half-salary payments, while pensioners allegedly went unpaid for more than four years. “We are therefore not surprised that ADC, harbouring birds of the same feather, cannot pay its workers’ salaries,” he said. Alake urged Nigerians and workers to reject the ADC, Atiku and all candidates running on the party’s platform in the next general elections. “We are sounding a warning to Nigerians and working people now: reject ADC. Reject Atiku Abubakar and reject all ADC candidates in the next general elections,” he said. He argued that a party seeking to govern Nigeria should be able to demonstrate responsible management of its own affairs and the welfare of its workforce. item.title: LAWMA begins expansion works at Olusosun dumpsite to boost waste evacuation
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos Waste Management Authority, LAWMA, has initiated critical stabilisation and expansion works on tipping platforms E1 and E2 at the Olusosun dumpsite in Ojota. ​The upgrade, executed in partnership with Zoomlion Nigeria Limited, aims to expand platform capacity, allow more waste collection trucks to discharge simultaneously, and significantly enhance operational safety and speed. ​Speaking at the agency’s headquarters in Ijora-Olopa on Monday, LAWMA Executive Director of Finance, Mr. Kunle Adebiyi, disclosed that construction on the site is progressing according to schedule. ​Adebiyi noted that the Olusosun upgrade is part of a broader infrastructure plan that includes ongoing improvements at other major dumping facilities, such as Solus III and Epe. “Together, these upgrades are expected to strengthen the state’s overall waste evacuation network, dramatically reduce truck turnaround times, and improve service delivery across Lagos,” he stated. ​To minimise disruption during the construction phase, Adebiyi appealed for cooperation from Private Sector Participation, PSP operators, waste truck drivers, and other key industry stakeholders. ​The agency therefore reaffirmed its commitment to upgrading waste management infrastructure and maintaining a cleaner, healthier environment for all residents of Lagos State. item.title: Arik Receivership: Court admits AMCON board resolutions
item.description: By Henry Ojelu The Lagos State Special Offences Court, Ikeja, on Monday admitted certified board resolutions of the Asset Management Corporation of Nigeria (AMCON) as evidence in the ongoing criminal trial of its former Managing Director, Ahmed Kuru, and others over the receivership of Arik Air Limited. Justice Mojisola Dada admitted the documents in a bench ruling, holding that they were relevant to the proceedings and duly certified in line with Section 104 of the Evidence Act, 2011. The documents were tendered by counsel to the second defendant, Mr Uyi Giwa-Osagie, to counter the claim by the fourth prosecution witness, Bawa Usman Kaltungo, that Kuru had unilaterally authorised the receivership. Kaltungo, head of the AMCON desk at the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, and leader of its investigating team, had maintained during cross-examination that Kuru, as AMCON’s managing director and chief executive officer, had unfettered powers and personally sanctioned the receivership. However, Giwa-Osagie tendered the certified board resolutions to establish that the decision was approved by AMCON’s board as a corporate body. The prosecution counsel, Dr Wahab Shittu, SAN, objected to the admissibility of the documents, arguing that they were too remote and irrelevant to the charges. But Giwa-Osagie argued that his client was not standing trial over the propriety of appointing a receiver but over other allegations contained in the charge sheet. He maintained that the documents went to the root of the case and were capable of establishing his client’s innocence. He also argued that they were public documents duly certified and tendered from the Bar. In her ruling, Justice Dada upheld their admissibility, noting that the resolutions emanated from AMCON’s board as a corporate body and had been certified in accordance with the law. The EFCC had arraigned Kuru; Kamilu Omokide, former receiver-manager of Arik Air; Captain Roy Ilegbodu, the airline’s chief executive officer; Union Bank Limited; and Super Bravo Limited over allegations arising from the airline’s receivership. The prosecution followed a petition by Mr Femi Falana, SAN, on behalf of Arik Air’s promoters and shareholders. The court adjourned the case until October 27, 2026, for continuation of trial. item.title: 2027 Polls: Don’t let politicians manipulate the law, CJN warns judges
item.description: By Ilechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja In anticipation of litigation that could arise from the 2027 general elections, the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, on Monday warned judges across the country against allowing politicians to manipulate the legal system to gain undeserved advantage. The CJN particularly urged heads of courts to remain vigilant against practices capable of undermining the integrity of judicial proceedings. She identified such practices as including forum shopping, concealment of related proceedings and attempts to obtain conflicting orders from courts of coordinate jurisdiction. Speaking during the opening session of the 2026 roundtable for heads of courts, organised by the National Judicial Institute (NJI) in Abuja, the CJN said the issues called for particular attention as the nation heads towards another election season. While acknowledging that election-related disputes usually attract intense public interest and considerable pressure on the courts, the CJN said the judiciary must be prepared to discharge its constitutional responsibilities with impartiality, courage and fidelity to the law. “Political sensitivity, public sentiment or the urgency with which a matter is presented must never displace the careful application of the Constitution, the Electoral Act and the applicable rules of court. “I urge your lordships to ensure that appropriate administrative arrangements are in place to facilitate the timely and orderly handling of election-related matters. “Judicial officers must be reminded of the need to scrutinise applications carefully, insist on full and frank disclosure of relevant facts, pay due regard to related proceedings and resist any attempt to use urgent applications or ex-parte orders to secure an improper advantage. “The integrity of judicial proceedings must not be compromised by competing political interests or pressure from any quarter. “Forum shopping is particularly damaging because it undermines consistency, encourages abuse of process and exposes the Judiciary to avoidable public controversy. “Your lordships must therefore ensure that existing procedural safeguards are observed and that appropriate steps are taken whenever attempts to circumvent established judicial processes come to light. “No litigant should be permitted to manipulate the judicial system in search of a favourable decision. Public confidence in the judiciary will be tested during this period,” she added. Moreover, Justice Kekere-Ekun reminded the heads of courts that they are expected to provide the leadership necessary to ensure that election-related cases are handled competently, expeditiously and strictly in accordance with the law. She said the objective is to ensure that the courts remain impartial arbiters of disputes, free from political influence and guided solely by the facts, the applicable law and the demands of justice. item.title: ‘Atiku majored in hygiene, cannot rule Nigeria’s modern economy’ — Shettima
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Vice President Kashim Shettima has criticised former vice president Atiku Abubakar over his proposal to restore fuel subsidy, questioning his ability to govern Nigeria’s modern economy. Shettima said Atiku’s proposal would push the country back into poverty, accusing the former vice president of supporting the return of subsidy for political reasons. Speaking at the Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja on Monday, Shettima said, “One of the leading presidential candidates is advocating for the return of the subsidy scheme. He wants us to backslide into penury for political convenience.” He also questioned Atiku’s professional background, referring to his training at the Kano School of Hygiene as he challenged his capacity to manage the country’s economy. “I dare to put forward that his skill set — he was trained in sanitation at the Kano School of Hygiene — so he doesn’t have the skill set to govern a modern economy. That’s the painful truth,” Shettima said. Shettima further questioned Atiku’s knowledge of environmental sanitation, using the difference between flu and Ebola to make his point. “Even his decisions in environmental sanitation, I do not think he can make a distinction between flu and even Ebola,” he said. Shettima urged Nigerians to assess the proposals and qualifications of political leaders before making decisions, warning against ignoring the implications of their choices. “Nigerians must have to decide and those of you here cannot afford to play the ostrich,” he added. Atiku has advocated the restoration of fuel subsidy as part of his proposed approach to managing the economy. The issue remains a major point of disagreement between the opposition and the administration of President Bola Tinubu, which removed the subsidy in May 2023. While the government has defended the removal as necessary to reduce the financial burden on public finances, the policy has been accompanied by higher fuel prices and increased living costs for many Nigerians. item.title: Five Things To Know Today
item.description: 1. Ebola patient evacuated to Switzerland as Nigeria continues monitoring contacts Nigeria’s first confirmed Ebola patient in the current regional outbreak has been medically evacuated from Abuja to Switzerland, following a significant improvement in her condition. Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate confirmed that the patient was stable, conscious, and communicating before departure. Her husband, a Swiss diplomat who has shown no symptoms, accompanied her. The transfer does not mean the patient is no longer infectious. Strict medical precautions remain necessary, and Swiss authorities will assume responsibility for her treatment. Nigeria continues monitoring 52 other contacts. Authorities say there are currently no confirmed Ebola patients remaining in the country, although contact tracing continues. Why it matters: The evacuation changes Nigeria’s immediate case-management responsibilities, but not the need to detect possible secondary infections. The primary source of the patient’s infection also remains unresolved. Watch : Test results among contacts, the outcome of investigations into the patient’s travel history and further updates from the NCDC and Africa CDC. 2. Code of Conduct Bureau investigates Obi, Saraki and David Mark over offshore assets This photo combo shows David Mark (left), Bukola Saraki (centre), and Peter Obi (right) The Code of Conduct Bureau has opened investigations into seven individuals named in earlier Panama Papers and Pandora Papers reporting, according to a new Premium Times investigation. Those identified include Peter Obi, former Senate Presidents Bukola Saraki and David Mark, and former Aviation Minister Stella Oduah. The inquiries concern alleged failures to declare offshore assets or business interests while holding public office. The investigations do not establish wrongdoing. Offshore company ownership is not inherently illegal; the relevant questions concern compliance with asset-declaration and public-office rules. Why it matters : The inquiries concern public-office accountability and include prominent political figures involved in Nigeria’s political landscape. Watch : Formal CCB statements, responses from those named, and whether any investigation leads to proceedings before the Code of Conduct Tribunal. 3. The Nigeria Democratic Congress has announced a 118-member National Campaign Council ahead of the January 2027 elections. Former Bayelsa Governor Henry Seriake Dickson will chair the council, with presidential candidate Peter Obi as co-chairman. Vice-presidential candidate Rabiu Kwankwaso is co-vice-chairman, while Ibrahim Abdulkarim has been named Director-General. The party scheduled the council’s formal inauguration for today in Abuja. item.title: Invest In Training, Boost Production To 3m/b Per Day, PETAN Urges Indigenous Oil Firms
item.description: The Petroleum Technology Association of Nigeria (PETAN) has urged indigenous oil and gas companies to invest in training young Nigerians and strengthening technical capacity to support the country’s ambition of producing three million barrels of crude oil per day. PETAN Chairman, Wole Ogunsanya, made the call at the association’s media roundtable in Lagos on Monday, warning that the transfer of oil and gas assets from international oil companies to indigenous operators had created an urgent need to train the next generation of industry professionals. He said Nigeria faced a widening gap between experienced oil and gas workers and younger professionals entering the industry, stressing that local operators must develop training programmes to sustain production and retain technical expertise. “We have a huge gap between those that are experienced in the industry versus age. Training is a very important aspect of our industry,” Ogunsanya said. PETAN Chairman, Wole Ogunsanya, while addressing journalists at a media roundtable in Lagos on Monday, October 26, 2026. He noted that many experienced Nigerian professionals had received their training through multinational companies, including Shell, ExxonMobil, Chevron and TotalEnergies, often benefiting from international placements and technical development programmes. However, he questioned whether similar opportunities would remain available as international operators divested some of their onshore, swamp and shallow-water assets. “Now we are divesting the assets. We are selling the assets to indigenous companies. Almost 100 per cent of the assets on land, in the swamp and shallow waters are owned by Nigerian indigenous companies. “Who is going to train the Nigerians? The new generation of Nigerians are coming behind to take over and operate those assets and work for these companies successfully,” he said. Training Centre Ogunsanya said Nigeria had sufficient human resources to develop its oil and gas industry, but needed to do more to attract graduates and provide them with practical skills. “The issue is not that we don’t have Nigerian young educated graduates that can come into the industry. The issue is how do we encourage these young educated Nigerian graduates to look into the oil and gas industry?” he asked. He said the industry required professionals with practical experience in drilling, pipeline installation, fabrication, welding and offshore operations, adding that training must prepare young Nigerians for the physical and technical demands of the sector. Ogunsanya disclosed that PETAN recruited nearly 100 engineers every two years through its internship programme, placing them in member companies for practical training. “After two years, PETAN members absorb over 60 per cent of these guys because that’s how good the training that we’re giving them is,” he said. item.title: Nigeria’s Index Ebola Patient, Husband Evacuated To Switzerland – Pate
item.description: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Ali Pate, on Monday confirmed that the first imported Ebola virus disease case in the country has been flown out of the country to Switzerland. Pate made the confirmation on his X handle, stating that the index patient, who has clinically improved, is stable and conscious, was evacuated along with her husband, who remained asymptomatic. He wrote: “I confirm that, with my approval, earlier this morning, the index case for Nigeria’s first imported Ebola virus disease departed Abuja for Switzerland. The index patient was clinically much improved, stable, conscious, communicating, and her clinical laboratory test results closing towards baseline. He, however, stated that her improvements do not mean she is not infectious, stating that strict protocols were put in place before her evacuation. “This does not mean she is not still infectious, hence the strict protocols in place. The patient was evacuated along with her spouse who has remained asymptomatic. ‘I thank all the various clinical staff for the high quality care they provided the patient as well as the public health personnel who ensured the evacuation was carried out in line with best public health measures for such evacuations. “We will provide further updates later this afternoon after the patient and her spouse lands successfully in their destination. “All public health measures are continuing to ensure successful containment of the imported virus. “I urge Nigerians to remain vigilant and rely on information from credible sources”, Pate said. The development came after the Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), on Sunday, said that the number of contacts linked to the index case of Ebola recorded in October 2026 had risen to 53. The agency said the contacts comprise health workers as well as the domestic staff and spouse of the patient diagnosed with the disease. The NCDC, in its Ebola Disease Situation Report, said that a newly suspected case was reported by Rivers State on October 23, but laboratory results returned negative for Ebola disease. “Fifty-three contacts linked to the index case have so far been identified, categorized and followed up. Contacts listed include healthcare workers, domestic staff and spouse,” the report dated October 24, 2026, partly read. Giving a background on the index case, it said the patient is a 42-year-old woman who returned from Uganda through Addis Ababa on October 3, 2026, via an international flight to Abuja, Nigeria. The agency said she became symptomatic four days later and presented to a private health facility on October 10, and another on October 11. “She presented to another private facility on the 11th of October 2026, where she was admitted.
